cards.name: Dust and Scratch
cards.summary: Noise clean-up: within a Radius of each pixel it smooths away specks and thin lines that differ from their neighbours by more than the Threshold, leaving broader edges alone. Pushed hard (big radius, low threshold) it melts fine detail into a flat, median-filtered, slightly painterly smear.
use_for: removing dust specks and hairline scratches from scanned photos and prints
cleaning compression noise from a low-quality video frame or web image before placing it in a layout
despeckling a bitmap before PowerTRACE so the trace has fewer stray nodes
light smoothing of skin or busy texture on a placed photo
avoid: A large Radius with a low Threshold wipes real detail: thin type, hairlines, eyelashes and jewellery vanish (on the test plate the thin white hairlines in the bottom strip vanish first and the corners of the white 'PGD 2026' type round off); raise Threshold until only the specks disappear.
It cannot rebuild scratches or tears wider than the radius; retouch those with a clone or healing tool in Corel PHOTO-PAINT or Photoshop.
Not a general blur and not a sharpener: for overall softening use a Blur effect, and sharpen afterwards with Unsharp Mask if edges went soft.
The scripted path needs a bitmap shape (Shape.Bitmap); convert vector art to a bitmap first, or apply from the Effects menu where it stays a non-destructive effect.

params.name: Radius
params.does: Size in pixels of the neighbourhood searched for specks; flaws narrower than about the radius are removed. Bigger = stronger, blotchier smoothing that also eats real detail.
params.typical: 1-3 for real dust (default 2); 8-20 only as a stylised smear

params.name: Threshold
params.does: How different (0-255 levels) a pixel must be from its neighbours before it is treated as a speck. Low = more pixels replaced, stronger clean-up; high = only very contrasty specks are touched.
params.typical: 20-64 (default 64); near 0 smooths everything inside the radius

pairs_with: Effects/Sharpen/Unsharp Mask (restore edge crispness after the clean-up)
Bitmaps > Outline Trace / PowerTRACE (trace the despeckled bitmap)
Effects/Noise/Tune Noise (compare other noise filters side by side)
cards.scripting: shape.Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect("Dust and Scratch", "DustScratchEffect Radius=10,Threshold=8")  (command format proven on other effects, not yet applied for this one; ApplyBitmapEffect returns OK even for a wrong string, so compare pixels before/after). Menu: Effects > Correction > Dust and Scratch (GUID b2e22b39-eb2b-4847-a3ed-fd14b8c79741).
cards.non_destructive: yes from the menu: CorelDRAW 2024 adds it to the object's effect stack (Properties docker > Effects), on bitmaps and vector objects, editable and removable later; the harvest does not record whether the scripted ApplyBitmapEffect call stacks or bakes the pixels
cards.cost: low: one median-style pass; slows with a large Radius on big bitmaps

review.changes: avoid: the test plate has 1-6 px hairlines and large 'PGD 2026' type, not small type; non_destructive true -> qualified string (menu route stacks; scripted ApplyBitmapEffect stack-or-bake not harvested)

verified.note: 1:1 crop: the thin hairlines vanish and the thicker ones merge into one white bar at the bottom, the swatch corners round off and the panel detail smooths into blobs while broad areas stay put: the hard-pushed median clean-up described (Radius 10 / Threshold 8).

previous.note: Fine thin features are smoothed away: the white PGD type melts into unreadable blobs and the bottom hairlines merge into one bar, while the mid-tones and stripes only soften slightly (body diff about 1), the median-like clean-up described, pushed hard at Radius 10 / Threshold 8.

cards.name: Tune Sharpen
cards.summary: A side-by-side 'tune' dialog for sharpening: it previews thumbnails of four sharpen filters (Unsharp Mask, Adaptive Unsharp, Sharpen, Directional Sharpen) and you click the variant you like, step by step, to build up crisper edges and local contrast. How exactly the Percentage and Background sliders feed those thumbnails was not confirmed by the harvest.
use_for: quickly comparing sharpening methods on a placed product shot or portrait
crisping a soft video frame or upscaled image before print
restoring edge snap after Dust and Scratch or resampling
avoid: Over-sharpening a soft or noisy image (like the test plate's video frame) brings out halos, JPEG blocks and grain; stop at the first step that looks crisp.

Scripted use is uncertain: the filter picks are enum keys (ImageNode_UnsharpMask, ImageNode_AdaptiveUnsharp, ImageNode_Sharpen, ImageNode_DirectionalSharpen) with no harvested values, so a script cannot reliably choose one and may change nothing; for a repeatable scripted sharpen use Effects > Sharpen > Unsharp Mask with explicit Percentage / Radius / Threshold.
Sharpening cannot restore real focus; a badly blurred photo stays blurred, just with crunchy edges.
The scripted path needs a bitmap shape (Shape.Bitmap).

scripts: no scripted form applies it (2026-10-13 probe (44 forms: ListSize plus per-step Effect_n / Step_n / Percentage_n / Level_n keys, the sub-effect command names, the dialog thumbnail guids, the data-source route): TuneSharpnessEffect accepted every form and changed no pixel); open the dialog (menu route) and pick the thumbnails by hand

params.name: Percentage
params.does: Strength of each sharpening step the thumbnails apply (by analogy with Tune Blur's Step; not confirmed). Higher = crisper edges and more halo.

params.name: Background
params.does: Meaning not confirmed by the harvest; probably limits how much flat, low-contrast background is sharpened (a threshold-like control). Leave at the default unless testing.

params.name: Unsharp Mask
params.does: Thumbnail / node for the Unsharp Mask variant: the dialog pick, not a numeric setting (values not harvested).

params.name: Adaptive Unsharp
params.does: Thumbnail / node for the Adaptive Unsharp variant (sharpens by local edge strength).

params.name: Sharpen
params.does: Thumbnail / node for the plain Sharpen variant.

params.name: Directional Sharpen
params.does: Thumbnail / node for the Directional Sharpen variant (sharpens along edge direction, fewer halos).

pairs_with: Dust and Scratch (clean first, then sharpen)
Effects/Sharpen/Unsharp Mask (scriptable, explicit control)
Effects/Blur/Tune Blur (the matching tune dialog for softening)

cards.name: Art Style
cards.summary: Machine-learning (neural network) style transfer: re-renders the bitmap in the manner of a chosen painting or artwork style, so a photo becomes a painted or illustrated image with that style's brushwork and palette while keeping its composition. The harvest found no dialog parameters it could bind, so the style choice and any strength controls are not described here.
use_for: turning a stock photo into a painted illustration for a poster background
giving a set of mixed photos one artistic look across a brochure or social series
quick 'artwork' variants of a hero image for mood boards
avoid: Faces, logos and small text get warped by the style; do not use on photos where likeness or legible signage matters (press or news images), or mask those areas out.

The scripted path can only send the bare string 'ArtStyleEffect' with no parameters: untested for this effect, and the one bare effect-id string tried in the harvest apply tests (InvertEffect) changed no pixels. At best a script gets whatever style the dialog last used; choose the style from the menu dialog.
Neural processing is heavy on big bitmaps; resample to the output size first.
For a controllable, repeatable painterly look use Effects > Art Strokes (Impressionist, Watercolor ...) or Photoshop's Oil Paint instead.
pairs_with: Effects/Correction/Dust and Scratch (clean noise first so the style does not amplify it)
PowerClip (keep the stylised photo inside a shape)
Transparency tool (blend the stylised copy over the original)
cards.scripting: shape.Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect("Art Style", "ArtStyleEffect")  (no parameters; untested for this effect, and the only bare effect-id string in the harvest apply tests changed nothing, so check pixels before/after). Menu: Effects > Creative > Art Style (GUID a625752d-50ad-4c1a-8ea2-2b45c67db957).
cards.non_destructive: yes from the menu: CorelDRAW 2024 adds it to the object's effect stack (Properties docker > Effects), on bitmaps and vector objects, editable and removable later; the harvest does not record whether the scripted ApplyBitmapEffect call stacks or bakes the pixels
cards.cost: high: neural-network inference, seconds to minutes on a large bitmap

review.changes: avoid/scripting: bare 'ArtStyleEffect' string flagged as unproven (the only bare-id apply test, InvertEffect, changed no pixels); non_destructive true -> qualified string (menu route stacks; scripted ApplyBitmapEffect stack-or-bake not harvested)

verified.note: The photo is re-rendered as a painted illustration: flat facets with dark contour lines, the palette pushed to grey-blue with the stripe reds kept, the swatches turned into soft painted pastels, the style-transfer painting look described (in the dialog's stored style).

cards.name: Crystalize
cards.summary: Breaks the image into irregular polygonal cells, each filled with one averaged colour, like looking through crystal facets; small Size gives a fine faceted texture, large Size a bold abstract patchwork of flat polygons with no outlines.
use_for: abstract faceted background built from a photo
abstracting a busy photo behind headline text
geometric / low-poly style poster texture
stylised transition or title frames
avoid: Destroys detail: faces, logos and small type become blobs at large Size; mask them out or apply to a duplicate.
Cells have no outlines; for leaded cells use Effects > Creative > Stained Glass, for regular square blocks use Effects > Distort > Pixelate.
The menu says 'Crystalize' but the scripted effect id is CrystallizeEffect (double l); the scripted path needs a bitmap shape.

params.name: Size
params.does: Average size of the crystal cells; larger = fewer, bigger flat polygons and less recognisable image.

pairs_with: Stained Glass (same cells with solder lines)
Gaussian Blur afterwards to soften cell edges for a background
Transparency tool (fade the faceted copy over the original)

cards.name: Fabric
cards.summary: Re-renders the image as textile: depending on Style it becomes crochet, needlepoint stitches, quilt patches, strings or tissue-paper collage, each element taking the colour of the image beneath. Size sets the stitch / patch size, Complete how much of the image is converted, Brightness the lightness of the fabric and Rotation the angle of the pattern. (The style list was not harvested; the names above are from the app's documentation, medium confidence.)
use_for: handmade / craft-fair poster texture
embroidered or knitted look for kids', festive and textile-brand designs
textile mock-up of a logo or icon after converting it to a bitmap
avoid: Small elements over a busy photo read as noise; simplify the image or raise Size.
Style values were not harvested, so a script cannot choose a style; set it in the dialog.
Fine type and faces are lost; apply behind text, never to it.
For a texture that keeps the image intact use a bitmap pattern fill with transparency, or Photoshop's Texturizer.

params.name: Style
params.does: Which textile is simulated (crochet, needlepoint, quilt, strings, tissue collage ...); enum values not harvested.

params.name: Size
params.does: Size of each stitch, patch or strand; bigger = coarser, more stylised.

params.name: Complete
params.does: Percentage of the image converted to fabric; below 100 lets parts of the original show through.

params.name: Brightness
params.does: Lightness of the rendered fabric.

params.name: Rotation
params.does: Angle of the stitch / patch pattern in degrees (5-degree steps on the compass wheel).

pairs_with: Frame (stitched or torn border to finish the textile look)
Artistic Text on top in a bold rounded face
Transparency tool (fade the fabric copy over the original photo)

cards.name: Frame
cards.summary: Puts a decorative edge frame around the bitmap, taken from a frame image (a preset from the frame library or a file you load); the frame can be recoloured, faded (Opacity), feathered, blended into the picture, scaled horizontally and vertically, flipped and rotated. The result is a brushed, torn or ornamental border painted over the picture's edges.
use_for: vintage or brushed photo edges for posters and invitations
framing a portrait for a certificate or greeting card
quick decorative border on social graphics
avoid: It needs a frame image: a preset (Presets / CurrentFrameImage) or a file path (File). The harvest could not read the defaults or the frame list (the data source only exists while the dialog is open), so scripted use without the dialog is unreliable.
The frame covers the image edges: keep faces, logos and text away from the outer 10-15 percent.

Square has no caption in the dialog; by analogy with Glass Block and Scatter it probably locks Vertical to Horizontal. How a frame image fits a non-square bitmap was not harvested, so check the corners on wide images.
For a clean geometric border use a vector rectangle outline or PowerClip instead; it stays editable and sharp at any print size.

params.does: Which saved frame preset to use (values not harvested).

params.name: File
params.does: Path of a frame image file to load instead of a preset.
params.typical: a frame from the frame library

params.name: Color
params.does: Colour of the frame.
params.typical: black or white, or a brand colour

params.name: Opacity
params.does: Opacity of the frame over the image (0-100).

params.name: Blur/Feather
params.does: Softens the frame's inner edge so it fades into the picture.

params.name: Blend
params.does: Merge mode of the frame with the image (values not harvested).

params.name: Horizontal
params.does: Horizontal scale of the frame, likely percent of the image width (1-140).

params.name: Vertical

params.name: VFlip

pairs_with: Fabric or Art Strokes effects (a frame finishes a stylised photo)
Effects/Creative/Vignette (softer edge darkening instead of an ornament)
PowerClip (place the framed photo inside a layout shape)

cards.name: Glass Block
cards.summary: Makes the image look as if seen through a wall of thick glass bricks: the picture is divided into a grid of rectangular blocks and each block shows a shifted, lens-distorted piece of what is behind it, so edges break into a stepped grid.
use_for: obscured-glass backdrop behind headline text
architectural or bathroom-window texture
abstract grid backgrounds from a photo
stylised obscuring of a busy background
avoid: Small blocks on a busy photo read as noise; use blocks large enough to see the grid (Block width/height of 40 or more on a 1920 px image; the unit is not harvested).
Faces and text stay partly recognisable; for real anonymising use Pixelate with a large cell or a solid cover.
For a rippled or frosted look rather than a brick grid use Scatter or Smoked Glass.

params.name: Block width
params.does: Width of each glass block; bigger = larger, more obvious bricks.

params.name: Block height
params.does: Height of each glass block.
params.typical: same as width for square bricks

params.name: Square
params.does: Locks block height to block width.

pairs_with: Smoked Glass (tint and soften the bricked image)
Transparency tool (fade the glass copy over a sharp original)
bold sans headline on top

cards.name: Mosaic
cards.summary: Turns the image into a tile mosaic: small irregular tiles, each filled with the colour of the image underneath, set on a background (grout) colour, with an optional vignette frame around the result. The exact tile shape was not checked in the harvest (medium confidence).

avoid: Detail and type vanish at large tile sizes; mask faces and text out.
Background Color is not part of the scripted command, so a script gets the dialog's current grout colour.
For square, grout-free blocks (censor or 8-bit look) use Effects > Distort > Pixelate; for irregular polygons without grout use Crystalize.

cards.name: Scatter
cards.summary: Scrambles the image by moving pixels a random distance up to the Horizontal and Vertical amounts, so edges dissolve into a grainy, spray-painted or frosted-glass jitter while the colours stay the same.
use_for: frosted / shower-glass texture over a photo

avoid: Large amounts make faces, type and logos unreadable; mask them out.
The pattern is random and there is no seed setting, so a particular scatter cannot be chosen or matched by a setting; not for results that must match exactly.
For a smooth soft blur use a Blur effect; for a tinted frosted panel use Smoked Glass.

params.name: Vertical
